name: Flagship Bay Area Candidates Review V1
scope: Small Bay Area flagship cluster for editorial review only
editorial_standards: No rankings, scores, rent claims, vacancy claims, or inventory-depth claims in public copy.
Do not treat representative buildings as the intelligence source.
Do not infer district identity from city-level relationships without separate editorial support.
Use nearby relationships as geography prompts until corpus and editorial review confirm commercial rationale.

reviewed_places.name: Mountain View
reviewed_places.identity_summary: Multi-district Silicon Valley commercial market with existing snapshot context and nearby relationships to Sunnyvale and Santa Clara.
weakest_riskiest_assumptions: Graph support is city-level and nearby-oriented, not proof of distinct commercial contrast.
Castro Street and Whisman references need district-level corpus review before public district claims.
Do not convert legacy nearby relationships into availability or inventory claims.
reviewed_places.recommended_public_use: Use as a nearby alternative and possible comparison anchor for Downtown Palo Alto or Castro-Whisman after district review.
reviewed_places.recommended_editorial_refinement: Separate walkable downtown Mountain View, Castro-Whisman/R&D corridor, and North Bayshore signals before writing public comparison copy.

reviewed_places.name: Sunnyvale
reviewed_places.identity_summary: Suburban commercial node in the same South Bay/Peninsula comparison corridor as Mountain View and Santa Clara.
weakest_riskiest_assumptions: The current signal mostly proves proximity, not built-form or tenant-fit differentiation.
District-level subareas such as Moffett Park, Peery Park, and downtown Sunnyvale need separate evidence before public use.
Avoid treating Sunnyvale as a single uniform office market.
reviewed_places.recommended_public_use: Use as a nearby alternative in Silicon Valley orientation; hold stronger comparison copy for editorial review.
reviewed_places.recommended_editorial_refinement: Identify whether the public page is about the city, Moffett/Peery-style R&D areas, or downtown Sunnyvale before selecting comparison phrasing.

reviewed_places.name: Santa Clara
reviewed_places.current_identity_signal_quality: high city-level scaffold; commercial specificity still needs review
reviewed_places.identity_summary: Multi-district South Bay commercial market with nearby relationships to Sunnyvale, Mountain View, and San Jose.
weakest_riskiest_assumptions: North Santa Clara and citywide Santa Clara should not be conflated.
Relationship data supports geography adjacency more than public commercial identity.
Avoid implying tech demand, campus quality, or current market strength without current corpus review.
reviewed_places.recommended_public_use: Use as a South Bay comparison candidate once district-level commercial identity is separated from citywide geography.
reviewed_places.recommended_editorial_refinement: Clarify North Santa Clara, Central Expressway, and San Jose edge patterns before public district integration.

reviewed_places.name: Palo Alto
reviewed_places.identity_summary: Peninsula city with distinct downtown, Stanford-adjacent, and research/campus patterns that should not be merged into one public identity.
weakest_riskiest_assumptions: No generated comparison-intelligence record currently supports public comparison copy.
City-level Palo Alto language can become hype-prone if not narrowed to a district.
Downtown Palo Alto is stronger than the city-level record for flagship editorial use.
reviewed_places.recommended_public_use: Use city-level Palo Alto as a parent geography; use Downtown Palo Alto as the actual flagship candidate.
reviewed_places.recommended_editorial_refinement: Keep city-level copy restrained and route flagship editorial work through Downtown Palo Alto and other specific commercial areas.

reviewed_places.name: Downtown Palo Alto
reviewed_places.identity_summary: Compact walkable Peninsula downtown for startup, venture-adjacent, professional service, and client-facing office users.
weakest_riskiest_assumptions: District node is not yet represented in Geography Graph V1, so relationships are editorial rather than graph-native.
Premium/startup language should stay grounded in walkability, Caltrain access, and professional-service context.
Avoid broad Silicon Valley prestige claims.
reviewed_places.recommended_public_use: Use as a flagship public comparison candidate after connecting the district to Geography Graph nodes.
reviewed_places.recommended_editorial_refinement: Add graph node and relationship records for Downtown Palo Alto, Mountain View/Castro-Whisman, Redwood City Downtown, and California Avenue.
